partners.mechanism_chain: WNT7A (HGNC:12827) —DISRUPTS→ WNT signaling pathway; WNT4 (HGNC:12831) —DISRUPTS→ WNT signaling pathway; WNT signaling pathway —LEADS_TO→ Mullerian duct agenesis (HP:0000001); WNT signaling pathway —LEADS_TO→ Hyperandrogenism (HP:0011213); WNT signaling pathway —LEADS_TO→ Limb malformations (HP:0001867). Dysregulation of this pathway leads to mullerian duct agenesis and hyperandrogenism in Fuhrmann syndrome (primarily WNT4) and mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism (WNT4, WNT7A), as well as limb malformations associated with Fuhrmann syndrome.

### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Santos syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.741)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3238698, Reactome:R-HSA-373080)

**Proposed mechanism:** WNT7A (HGNC:12786) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (R-HSA-6809884); Wnt signaling pathway (R-HSA-6809884) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of limbs (HP:0004697); Wnt signaling pathway (R-HSA-6809884) —LEADS_TO→ Craniofacial abnormalities (HP:0000252). Loss-of-function variants in WNT7A disrupt the Wnt signaling pathway, leading to both limb and craniofacial abnormalities observed in Fuhrmann syndrome and Santos syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct causal genes for Fuhrmann syndrome and Santos syndrome, or demonstration that pathogenic variants in WNT7A lead to divergent downstream pathways or phenotypes that cannot be reconciled by a single mechanistic model. _(variant: Identification of common WNT7A variants (AF > 0.1%) in gnomAD with no associated phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in WNT7A offers potential for unified therapeutic strategies targeting Wnt signaling for both Fuhrmann syndrome and Santos syndrome, although the specific clinical manifestations may differ due to other genetic or environmental modifiers.

#### 2. phocomelia, Schinzel type  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.740)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3238698, Reactome:R-HSA-373080)

**Proposed mechanism:** WNT7A (HGNC:12786) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP436); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP436) —LEADS_TO→ Limb malformation (HP:0001159); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP436) —LEADS_TO→ Limb hypoplasia (HP:0001156); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP436) —LEADS_TO→ Anomalous limb development (HP:0002724); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP436) —LEADS_TO→ Shortening of the limb (HP:0005851); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP436) —LEADS_TO→ Phocomelia (HP:0001151). Loss-of-function mutations in WNT7A disrupt the Wnt signaling pathway, leading to a spectrum of limb malformations, including Fuhrmann syndrome and phocomelia, Schinzel type.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in WNT7A who do not exhibit any limb malformations would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome allele frequency > 0.01 for pathogenic WNT7A variants in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in WNT7A can enable the development of targeted therapies or interventions for limb malformations in both Fuhrmann syndrome and phocomelia, Schinzel type, potentially by modulating Wnt signaling.

#### 3. autosomal dominant Robinow syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.482)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3238698, Reactome:R-HSA-373080)

**Proposed mechanism:** WNT7A variant (MONDO:0009232) —DISRUPTS→ WNT7A (HGNC:12510); WNT7A (HGNC:12510) —DISRUPTS→ WNT signaling pathway (WP:0007257); WNT signaling pathway (WP:0007257) —LEADS_TO→ Fuhrmann syndrome (MONDO:0009232); WNT signaling pathway (WP:0007257) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000001); WNT5A variant (MONDO:0024455) —DISRUPTS→ WNT5A (HGNC:12507); WNT5A (HGNC:12507) —DISRUPTS→ WNT signaling pathway (WP:0007257); WNT signaling pathway (WP:0007257) —LEADS_TO→ Autosomal dominant Robinow syndrome 1 (MONDO:0024455); WNT signaling pathway (WP:0007257) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal genitalia (HP:0000027). Disruption of either WNT7A (Fuhrmann syndrome) or WNT5A (Robinow syndrome) leads to dysregulation of the shared WNT signaling pathway, ultimately causing overlapping phenotypes such as skeletal abnormalities and abnormal genitalia.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in WNT7A in individuals diagnosed with Fuhrmann syndrome, or absence of pathogenic variants in WNT5A in individuals diagnosed with autosomal dominant Robinow syndrome 1, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if genetic studies show no overlap in affected individuals or families, this would also weaken the proposed link. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing common variants in WNT7A or WNT5A that are not associated with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of WNT signaling in these distinct syndromes could inform therapeutic strategies targeting common downstream effectors for developmental abnormalities. For instance, interventions aimed at modulating WNT pathway activity might offer a unified approach to treating certain overlapping features of these conditions.

#### 4. mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.434)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3238698, Reactome:R-HSA-373080)

**Proposed mechanism:** WNT7A (HGNC:12827) —DISRUPTS→ WNT signaling pathway; WNT4 (HGNC:12831) —DISRUPTS→ WNT signaling pathway; WNT signaling pathway —LEADS_TO→ Mullerian duct agenesis (HP:0000001); WNT signaling pathway —LEADS_TO→ Hyperandrogenism (HP:0011213); WNT signaling pathway —LEADS_TO→ Limb malformations (HP:0001867). Loss-of-function mutations in either WNT7A or WNT4 disrupt the WNT signaling pathway, which is crucial for the development of the reproductive tract and limbs. Dysregulation of this pathway leads to mullerian duct agenesis and hyperandrogenism in Fuhrmann syndrome (primarily WNT4) and mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism (WNT4, WNT7A), as well as limb malformations associated with Fuhrmann syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in WNT7A or WNT4 in individuals with Fuhrmann syndrome or mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism, respectively, would support this hypothesis. Conversely, the absence of such variants, or the presence of variants in genes entirely unrelated to WNT signaling, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Pathogenic loss-of-function variants in WNT7A or WNT4 are absent or extremely rare in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of WNT signaling in these two developmental disorders could lead to insights into common therapeutic targets or diagnostic approaches for conditions affecting reproductive and limb development.
